findings.message: 'TIMEZONE' is not a grok pattern. Logstash refuses to compile an unknown name, so the filter never registers and EVERY line fails to parse - not just the ones this capture touches. Use a defined pattern: NUMBER or BASE10NUM for a decimal, HOSTNAME for a domain, NOTSPACE for anything without a space.

findings.message: the pattern matches 8 of 12 sample lines. It must match every one: a line it misses is dropped entirely, not partly parsed. The first it misses is '2026-10-30T20:50:32.872568+00:00 mail01 sendmail[64]: 69UKoUGI000063: to=<rui@lab.example>, delay=00:00:01, xdelay=00:00:01, mailer=local, pri=30395, dsn=2.0.0,'. Of the 4 patterns, the closest to it is '^%{TIMESTAMP_ISO8601:timestamp} %{HOSTNAME:host} (?<program>sendmail)\\[%{INT:pid}\\]: (?<queue_id>[0-9A-Za-z]{14}): to=<%'. the pattern matches up to %{GREEDYDATA:stat}, which fails on 'stat=Sent' It also misses lines of other shapes: '2026-10-30T20:50:34.387894+00:00 mail01 sendmail[66]: 69UKoX4S000066: ruleset=check_rcpt, arg1=<victim@gmail.com>, relay=r7-ws211.r3-net [17'; '2026-10-30T20:50:27.880004+00:00 mail01 sendmail[60]: 69UKoP7v000059: to=<ana@lab.example>, delay=00:00:01, xdelay=00:00:01, mailer=local, p'; '2026-10-30T20:50:37.889888+00:00 mail01 sendmail[68]: 69UKoZmR000067: to=<monitor@lab.example>, delay=00:00:01, xdelay=00:00:01, mailer=loca'. If this line is a VARIANT of the others - an extra word, a field that is sometimes absent - make that part optional with (?:...)? rather than writing a second pattern. If it is a DIFFERENT KIND of message - different words, not one more of them - add a pattern for it to `alternatives`, reusing the same capture name for the same value.
